title: Silent Hill
wiki_lead:
Silent Hill (Japanese: サイレントヒル, Hepburn: Sairento Hiru) is a Japanese horror franchise centered on a series of survival horror video games created by Team Silent and published by Konami. The franchise is primarily set in Silent Hill, a fictional American town plagued by supernatural events, the occult, and dreams manifested into physical form, often taking the shape of horrific environments and creatures stalking the protagonists. The series is heavily influenced by the literary genre of psychological horror, with its player characters being mostly "everymen". The franchise has expanded to include various printed works, three film adaptations, and various spin-off games.
The first four games (Silent Hill, Silent Hill 2, Silent Hill 3, and Silent Hill 4: The Room) were developed from 1999 to 2004 by Team Silent, a Japanese development team within Konami, and received critical acclaim. The next four games (Silent Hill: Origins, Silent Hill: Homecoming, Silent Hill: Shattered Memories and Silent Hill: Downpour) were developed from 2007 to 2012 by Western companies, but garnered much less positive reviews. P.T. was released in 2014 and received critical acclaim, which revealed a new game, Silent Hills being developed by Kojima Productions, a Japanese development team within Konami at that time. The game was cancelled in 2015 and the franchise went dormant for nearly 10 years. Since then, Konami has revived the series in 2022 with new entries such as Silent Hill: The Short Message, the remake of Silent Hill 2, Silent Hill f, Silent Hill: Townfall, and the upcoming remake of the first game.
As of September 2026, the games have collectively sold over 19.2 million copies worldwide.

Overview


Main series


Silent Hill (1999)

The first installment in the series follows Harry Mason as he searches for his missing adopted daughter in the mysterious Maine town of Silent Hill. Stumbling upon a cult conducting a ritual to revive a deity it worships, Harry discovers his daughter's true origin. Multiple game endings are possible depending on the in-game actions taken by the player. The game was released in 1999 for the PlayStation. In 2009, it became available for download from the European PlayStation Network store for the PlayStation 3 and the PlayStation Portable, and later that year from the North American PlayStation Network store.


Silent Hill 2 (2001)

The second installment in the series follows James Sunderland as he searches for his deceased wife Mary in Silent Hill after receiving a letter supposedly from her, informing him that she is waiting for him there. After searching and exploring the mysterious town, he ultimately realizes the true nature of her death. The game was released in September 2001 for the PlayStation 2. An extended version of the game was released for the Xbox in December of the same year as Silent Hill 2: Restless Dreams in North America and Silent Hill 2: Inner Fears in Europe, and for the PlayStation 2 in 2003 as Silent Hill 2
grok_lead: Silent Hill is a Japanese survival horror video game franchise created by director Keiichiro Toyama and developed primarily by Team Silent, a group within Konami Computer Entertainment Tokyo, and published by Konami. The series debuted with its self-titled first installment on February 23, 1999, for the PlayStation console in North America, centering on the fictional town of Silent Hill in the United States where protagonists encounter psychological manifestations of their personal traumas amid fog-shrouded streets and grotesque monsters. The franchise's core narrative revolves around the town's supernatural properties, which trap individuals in nightmarish alternate realities reflecting their guilt, regrets, and inner demons, often tied to a cult worshiping ancient deities. Over its 27-year history as of 2026, Silent Hill has produced eight mainline games, including acclaimed entries like Silent Hill 2 (2001), which explores themes of loss and denial through protagonist James Sunderland's search for his deceased wife, Silent Hill 3 (2003), focusing on a young woman's ties to the town's cult origins, Silent Hill 4: The Room (2004), and Silent Hill: Origins (2007). Later titles, developed by external studios after Team Silent's disbandment in 2004, such as Silent Hill: Homecoming (2008) by Double Helix Games and Silent Hill: Downpour (2012) by Vatra Games, expanded the lore while maintaining the series' emphasis on atmospheric tension and moral ambiguity. Gameplay in the Silent Hill series blends third-person exploration, puzzle-solving, and combat against otherworldly creatures, with limited resources heightening vulnerability and dread; fog obscures visibility to build suspense, while radio static alerts players to nearby threats. Sound design, led by composer Akira Yamaoka, features industrial noise, haunting melodies, and eerie silence to immerse players in psychological unease, distinguishing the series from action-oriented horror like Resident Evil. Recent revivals include the Silent Hill 2 remake by Bloober Team, initially released on October 8, 2024, for PlayStation 5 and PC, with the Xbox Series X/S version following on November 21, 2025, which preserves the original's somber tone with updated graphics and 3D audio. In September 2025, Silent Hill f, developed by NeoBards Entertainment and set in 1960s Japan, introduced a new story of a girl navigating a fog-enshrouded hometown influenced by Japanese folklore and societal pressures. In February 2026, Konami revealed Silent Hill: Townfall, a psychological horror game developed by Screen Burn (formerly No Code Studios) in co-production with Annapurna Interactive and published by Konami, featuring a first-person perspective, which was released on September 24, 2026, for PlayStation 5 and PC. Beyond video games, Silent Hill has expanded into other media, including two live-action films: Silent Hill (2006), directed by Christophe Gans and loosely adapting elements from the first two games, and its sequel Silent Hill: Revelation (2012). Director Christophe Gans has confirmed that a 4K restoration of the 2006 Silent Hill film is planned, using the original film negative for improved quality. He stated it is in the planning stages, with elements being gathered, and will likely accompany the home video release of Return to Silent Hill (2026). No specific release date, publisher, or Blu-ray edition has been officially announced yet. A third film, Return to Silent Hill, adapting Silent Hill 2 and directed by Gans, was released theatrically in the United States on January 23, 2026. The franchise also includes comic books, novels, and merchandise, with spin-offs like Silent Hill: The Arcade (2007) and the influential P.T. demo (2014), a teaser for the canceled Silent Hills collaboration between Konami and Hideo Kojima that impacted modern horror design.
